title: Security Review for OT/IT AI Assistants
summary: Adversarial testing and architecture review for AI assistants that read historian data, manuals and work orders, covering prompt injection, unsafe advice, data leakage and tool permissions.

seo.title: Security Review for OT/IT AI Assistants | VipraTech
seo.description: Security testing for plant and utility AI copilots: prompt injection, unsafe advice, data leakage and tool permissions, with evidence and retest.

designed_for: CISO or Head of OT Security

problem.intro: Utilities, mines and plants are piloting AI assistants that summarise alarms, answer questions from OEM manuals, draft work orders and query historian data. These assistants sit close to the IT/OT boundary and take instructions from the text they read, which creates risks a conventional VAPT does not cover.

pain_points.title: Assistants straddle the IT/OT boundary
pain_points.detail: A copilot that reads historian tags and writes to the CMMS can become a path across zones the network design was meant to keep apart.

pain_points.title: Instructions hidden in documents
pain_points.detail: Indirect prompt injection through a vendor manual, work order or email can change what the assistant says or does.

pain_points.title: Unsafe procedural answers
pain_points.detail: An assistant that can be talked into skipping isolation steps or bypassing an interlock is a safety issue, not just a security bug.

pain_points.title: Tool permissions grow quietly
pain_points.detail: Read-only pilots acquire write access to tickets, notifications or scripts as features are added, without fresh review.

solution.overview: We run a structured security review of the assistant before it reaches plant users, and again after significant changes. We map its data flows, tools and identities against your OT zones, then build test playbooks for your setting: direct and indirect prompt injection, jailbreaks aimed at unsafe procedures, leakage of network diagrams, credentials and personal data, and misuse of every tool the assistant can call. Our multi-agent test framework runs these playbooks against a staging instance, never live control systems. Security engineers validate each finding, record reproduction steps and evidence, propose fixes and retest once you have remediated.
capabilities: Architecture and data-flow review against your IT/OT zones and conduits
Direct and indirect prompt injection tests through manuals, work orders, emails and tickets
Unsafe-procedure tests such as skipping isolation, bypassing interlocks or silencing alarms
Tool and permission review for least privilege and read-only access to OT data
Leakage tests for network diagrams, credentials, plant drawings and personal data
Evidence pack mapped to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, NIST AI RMF and IEC 62443 concepts

workflow.title: Agree scope and rules
workflow.detail: We agree the assistant, environment, test windows and rules of engagement with your OT and IT security teams.

workflow.title: Map data flows and tools
workflow.detail: We document what the assistant reads, which tools it can call, which identities it uses and where it crosses zone boundaries.

workflow.title: Run test campaigns
workflow.detail: The test framework runs adversarial playbooks against the staging instance and records every prompt, response and tool call.

workflow.title: Validate findings
workflow.detail: A security engineer reproduces each candidate finding and assesses its real impact.

workflow.title: Report with fixes
workflow.detail: Findings are reported with severity, evidence and specific remediation such as permission changes, input filtering or prompt and retrieval fixes.

workflow.title: Retest
workflow.detail: After remediation we rerun the relevant playbooks and close findings with evidence.

faqs.q: Will your testing touch our live SCADA or DCS?
faqs.a: No. We test a staging or replica instance of the assistant with synthetic data, under signed rules of engagement. If the assistant has any path to live OT, that path is itself a finding we report.

faqs.q: How is this different from our annual VAPT?
faqs.a: A VAPT tests networks and applications for known vulnerability classes. This review tests how the AI behaves: whether text it reads can change its instructions, whether it gives unsafe procedural advice and whether its tools can be misused. The two complement each other.

faqs.q: What do you need from us to start?
faqs.a: Architecture diagrams, the assistant's prompts and tool definitions, a staging instance with test accounts and a contact in OT security. Sample documents help us build realistic injection tests.

faqs.q: Can the tests be repeated after changes?
faqs.a: Yes. Playbooks are kept as a regression suite, so the same tests run after model, prompt or tool changes, and results are compared with the previous round.
